title: Canonical derived comparison for bar reindexing
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a small category and $R$ a commutative ring. Write $\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{op},\operatorname{Mod}_R)$; it is the module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] for the constant ring on the topology generated by singleton identities [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Derived categories and cochain complexes mean [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Here left $V$-acyclic means that the canonical comparison $LV(M[0])\to V(M)[0]$ is an isomorphism for the object $M$ in question. For $U\in\mathcal E$ and an $R$-module $M$, put $L_U(M)(V)=\bigoplus_{a:V\to U}M$, with restriction along $b:W\to V$ sending $(a,m)$ to $(ab,m)$. For $F\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}$, let $B_{\mathcal E,R}(F)^{-n}=\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}L_{U_n}(F(U_0))$ for $n\ge0$, with zero positive terms. On evaluation at $V$ its generators are $(V\xrightarrow a U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$. The face $d_j$ deletes $U_{n-j}$, composing adjacent arrows (including $a$ when $j=0$); the last face restricts $x$ along $U_1\to U_0$. Use differential $\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jd_j$ for $n>0$, and augmentation $a_F(a:V\to U_0,x)=F(a)x$ in degree zero. Put $C_{\mathcal E,R}=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal E^{op}}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Write $K_{\mathcal E,R}(F)^{-n}=\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}F(U_0)$, zero in positive degrees, with differential $\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jd_j$ deleting $U_{n-j}$, composing at internal vertices and restricting the coefficient only for $j=n$. Let $u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ be a functor of small categories, $G\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal D,R}$ and $t:F\to u^{-1}G$ a natural map, with $u^{-1}$ denoting precomposition. Suppose the displayed bar augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms, the terms of $B_{\mathcal E,R}(F)$ are left acyclic for $C_{\mathcal E,R}$ and $u_!$, and the terms of $u_!B_{\mathcal E,R}(F)$ and $B_{\mathcal D,R}(G)$ are left $C_{\mathcal D,R}$-acyclic. Suppose the total left derived functors are defined everywhere [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization] with canonical comparisons $\varepsilon$ and the derived adjunctions to exact precomposition. Here normalized derived adjunction means that, for every ordinary chain map $f:u_!C\to N$, the map $Q(f)\varepsilon_C$ has adjunct $Q(f^\flat)$, with the analogous condition for each colimit-constant adjunction. Then
$$m_F=Q(b_F)\,\varepsilon_{B(F)}\,LC_{\mathcal E,R}(Qa_F)^{-1}:LC_{\mathcal E,R}(F[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}QK_{\mathcal E,R}(F)$$
is a natural isomorphism in $D(R)$, where $b_F:CB(F)\cong K(F)$ is the coefficientwise colimit identification and $Q$ is localization. The formula $(V\xrightarrow a U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)\mapsto(uV\xrightarrow{u(a)}uU_n\to\cdots\to uU_0,t_{U_0}x)$ defines an augmentation-compatible chain map $B_{\mathcal E,R}(F)\to u^{-1}B_{\mathcal D,R}(G)$. Its adjunct $u_!B(F)\to B(G)$ represents the derived adjunct $Lu_!(F[0])\to G[0]$ of $t$. Under $m_F,m_G$ the canonical map $LC_{\mathcal E,R}(F[0])\cong LC_{\mathcal D,R}Lu_!(F[0])\to LC_{\mathcal D,R}(G[0])$ is the chain map $(U_\bullet,x)\mapsto(uU_\bullet,t_{U_0}x)$. The comparison $LC_{\mathcal D,R}Lu_!\cong LC_{\mathcal E,R}$ here is the one obtained by composing adjunctions; on these bar models it is the identity identification $C_{\mathcal D,R}u_!B(F)\cong C_{\mathcal E,R}B(F)$, including the derived units. In particular its normalization is fixed by the ordinary unit $B(F)\to u^{-1}\pi_{\mathcal D}^{-1}C_{\mathcal D,R}u_!B(F)$, with $\pi_{\mathcal D}^{-1}$ the constant functor.

proof.text: Write $B=B_{\mathcal E,R}(F)$, $B'=B_{\mathcal D,R}(G)$, $U=u_!$, $C=C_{\mathcal E,R}$, $D=C_{\mathcal D,R}$, $r=u^{-1}$, and $k_{\mathcal E},k_{\mathcal D}$ for constant functors. The presheaf categories are abelian; the representable-sum lemma supplies enough projectives, also for $\operatorname{Mod}_R$. The three left adjoints are additive and right exact: their Hom bijections are linear, and applying them to a cokernel identifies its Hom into any target with the kernel of precomposition, hence identifies its image with the cokernel of the image map. The bars and $UB$ vanish in positive degrees. Their assumed termwise acyclicity therefore lets the bounded-above computation lemma give isomorphisms $e=\varepsilon^U_B:LU(QB)\to QUB$, $p=\varepsilon^C_B:LC(QB)\to QCB$, $q=\varepsilon^D_{UB}:LD(QUB)\to QDUB$, and $q'=\varepsilon^D_{B'}:LD(QB')\to QDB'$.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), acyclic resolution computation; dual of Tag 015E (derived-lemma-leray-acyclicity).

proof.text: The augmented-bar lemma gives the natural chain isomorphisms $b_F:CB\cong K(F)$ and $b_G:DB'\cong K(G)$ with their specified coefficients. Since $Qa_F$ and $Qa_G$ are invertible, step 1 makes $m_F=Qb_F\,p\,LC(Qa_F)^{-1}$ and $m_G=Qb_G\,q'\,LD(Qa_G)^{-1}$ isomorphisms. Naturality is exactly the augmented-resolution naturality equation of the computation lemma followed by naturality of $b$: for $s:F\to H$, $K(s)$ multiplies each coefficient by $s_{U_0}$ and $QK(s)m_F=m_HLC(s[0])$.

Let $\ell:B\to rB'$ be the displayed generator map. Restriction along $b:W\to V$ replaces $a$ by $ab$ on both sides because $u(ab)=u(a)u(b)$. Every face except the last commutes with $\ell$ by preservation of composition by $u$; the last commutes because $t_{U_1}F(c)=G(u(c))t_{U_0}$ for $c:U_1\to U_0$. The alternating sums therefore commute too. In degree zero $G(u(a))t_{U_0}x=t_VF(a)x$, so $(ra_G)\ell=t[0]a_F$. This proves both the chain-map and augmentation assertions, with the same signs in all degrees.

source.place: Tag 08PH (example-morphism-categories), verification of the displayed chain formula.

proof.text:
Let $f:UB\to B'$ be the ordinary adjunct of $\ell$. The given normalization says that $Qf\,e$ has derived adjunct $Q\ell$. Naturality of the Hom bijection, first in the target and then in the source, shows that
$$\delta=Qa_G\,Qf\,e\,LU(Qa_F)^{-1}:LU(F[0])\to G[0]$$
has adjunct $Q(ra_G)Q\ell\,(Qa_F)^{-1}=Q(t[0])$. Thus $f$ represents precisely the specified derived adjunct, with the computation isomorphism $e\,LU(Qa_F)^{-1}$, not a separately chosen isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08PD (remark-morphism-fibred-categories), explicit adjunct using the normalization hypothesis.

proof.text:
Let $\eta^U,\eta^D,\eta^C$ be the ordinary units. The composite-adjunction formula and $rk_{\mathcal D}=k_{\mathcal E}$ give the unit-preserving natural isomorphism $c:DU\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ of the common-left-adjoint uniqueness lemma. Its defining equation is
$$k_{\mathcal E}(c_B)\,r(\eta^D_{UB})\,\eta^U_B=\eta^C_B.$$
Consequently $c_B$ is the ordinary colimit identification: its inverse sends the cocone element of $z\in B(V)$ to the cocone element of $\eta^U_B(z)$ in $(UB)(uV)$. Equality here is checked after the coprojections of $CB$, which jointly determine maps by the colimit universal property. Let $\beta:LD\,LU\xrightarrow{\sim}LC$ be the analogous unit-preserving derived comparison.

The required normalization of $\beta$ is
$$p\,\beta_{QB}=Q(c_B)\,q\,LD(e).$$
Transpose both sides under $LD\,LU\dashv rk_{\mathcal D}$. The left transpose is $Q\eta^C_B$, by unit compatibility of $\beta$ and the assumed normalization for $C\dashv k_{\mathcal E}$ applied to $1_{CB}$. For the right side, the first transpose, under $LD\dashv k_{\mathcal D}$, is
$$Q\bigl(k_{\mathcal D}(c_B)\,\eta^D_{UB}\bigr)\,e.$$
Indeed, naturality of this Hom bijection in its source moves $LD(e)$ to precomposition by $e$, while its normalization applied to $c_B:DUB\to CB$ gives the remaining factor. Set $h=k_{\mathcal D}(c_B)\,\eta^D_{UB}:UB\to k_{\mathcal D}CB$, an ordinary chain map. The second transpose, under $LU\dashv r$, is $Q(h^\flat)=Q(r(h)\eta^U_B)$ by the assumed normalization for $U$. Since $rk_{\mathcal D}=k_{\mathcal E}$, this is $Q(k_{\mathcal E}(c_B)\,r(\eta^D_{UB})\,\eta^U_B)=Q\eta^C_B$ by step 5. Injectivity of the composite Hom bijection proves the equality, including both derived units.

source.place: Tags 08PD/08PH (remark-morphism-fibred-categories, example-morphism-categories), two successive normalized transposes.

proof.text:
The canonical map in the statement is $\gamma=LD(\delta)\,\beta_{F[0]}^{-1}$. Substitute step 4 into $m_G\gamma$. Naturality of $\varepsilon^D$ gives $q'LD(Qf)=Q(Df)q$; step 6 gives $qLD(e)=Q(c_B)^{-1}p\beta_{QB}$. Finally naturality of $\beta$ gives $\beta_{QB}LDLU(Qa_F)^{-1}=LC(Qa_F)^{-1}\beta_{F[0]}$. Cancelling $LD(Qa_G)^{-1}LD(Qa_G)$ and $\beta_{F[0]}\beta_{F[0]}^{-1}$ yields
$$m_G\gamma=Q\bigl(b_G(Df)c_B^{-1}b_F^{-1}\bigr)m_F.$$
All inverse maps used here are isomorphisms from steps 1--2 or the common-adjoint comparison, so the cancellations take place in $D(R)$.

source.place: Tags 08PD/08PH (remark-morphism-fibred-categories, example-morphism-categories), substitution and naturality of the canonical comparisons.

proof.text: In degree $-n$, a generator $(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$ of $K(F)$ is $b_F$ of the colimit class of $(1_{U_n}:U_n\to U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$ in $B(U_n)$. Step 5 sends it under $c_B^{-1}$ to the class of its image by $\eta^U_B$ at $uU_n$. The ordinary adjunct equation $(rf)\eta^U_B=\ell$ then sends it under $Df$ to the class of $(1_{uU_n}:uU_n\to uU_n\to\cdots\to uU_0,t_{U_0}x)$. The coefficient identification $b_G$ sends this to $(uU_n\to\cdots\to uU_0,t_{U_0}x)$. Direct-sum generators determine these linear maps. Thus the chain map in step 7 is exactly the asserted reindexing map. Step 6 fixes the composite comparison by the ordinary composite unit, proving the final normalization clause as well.
